newsitem.title: USA: MSRB aide estimates par value of muni issue trades.
newsitem.headline: MSRB aide estimates par value of muni issue trades.

text.p: The par value of issues traded in the municipal bond market -- in both the interdealer and dealer-customer markets -- may total roughly $800 billion annually, MSRB's top staffer said, stressing the figure is a "very, very rough guess."
"Total interdealer volume on an annual basis is about $360 billion," Christopher Taylor, executive director of Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board, said at a press briefing.
"That might go to $800 billion on an annual basis" when trades between dealers and customers are added, Taylor said. "That's a little more than doubling."
Taylor said volume figures are beginning to take shape for all municipal trading as the MSRB gradually pieces together its transaction reporting program initiated in January 1995.
Phase one of the program, under which dealers report price information from interdealer trades, started July 1.
The next phase, where dealers will report price information for the first time on institutional and retail trades, takes full effect Jan 1, 1998.
The program is designed to make price data from municipal bond transactions available to the public and federal enforcement officials.
"We are as regulators coming under pressure to release more and more data and make it more widely available," Taylor said. "That is a positive for the industry and investors."
Taylor said dealer firms are helping MSRB develop the next phase of its transaction reporting program.

"A number of firms are beginning to supply us with sample data so we can begin to answer some of the questions (about total volume)," he said. "We are thrilled with the cooperation from industry to put this together. Everyone in the industry realizes the benefits," Taylor said.
Roger Hayes, MSRB's new chairman, said board members will visit bond firms nationwide between January and June to help them put their transaction reporting programs in place.
Taylor noted mandatory testing of the next phase of the program is scheduled to begin in July 1996.

"We are trying to give people the most information they possibly can get to make informed decisions about buying municipal bonds," said Hayes, managing director of municipal finance for NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc.
